archetype.name: Dual-Threat (power runner)
archetype.definition: A big-armed passer who hunts explosive throws downfield and uses his 237-pound frame as the offense's short-yardage and goal-line runner, with scrambles that turn broken plays into first downs.

report.headline: Arm and legs both top-tier; the rushing touchdowns are the part that cools.
report.take:
Allen is six games into another season where he is both the passing game and the power run game. His 8.8 yards per attempt ranks 3rd of 45 qualifiers, his 0.29 EPA per dropback ranks 6th, and his 240 rushing yards lead the position. The profile is the one he has carried for years: top-five rushing ranks in most seasons since 2018 and efficiency that has sat near the top of the league since 2020. Not much here is new.

The shape of the passing game has shifted a little. Last year he was a short-area distributor, with a 7.1 aDOT and 11.3% aggressiveness. This year his intended air yards are 8.65, aggressiveness is 12.87%, and yards per attempt is up 0.83 even though completion rate is down 2.6 points. The deep ball carries much of that. On 26 throws of 20+ air yards he is at 0.823 EPA per attempt with 4 touchdowns, completing only 38.5%. Keon Coleman has become the vertical outlet at 0.959 EPA per target, close to triple Shakir's or Kincaid's rate. The cost sits on the same throws: 3 of his 4 interceptions came on those deep shots. That is the gunslinger trade, and right now it pays clearly.

The numbers hide two things. First, the rushing scoring is lopsided. Six of his eight rushing touchdowns came on designed runs that average 2.48 yards a carry. He is the goal-line hammer, which also explains a red-zone passing line that looks bad (-0.051 EPA, 48.4% completions): the Bills run him in rather than throw. Second, the sacks. He is pressured on only 17.7% of dropbacks (10th), but 31.3% of those pressures end in a sack (26th of 37). That follows last year's 40.4% after years in the teens, so it is becoming a trait rather than a blip. It comes from holding the ball (2.97 seconds) to create. The return is 17 scrambles worth 1.247 EPA apiece with 12 first downs, which more than pays for the sacks.

One more piece of context: the Bills defense ranks 30th in EPA, and all but one of his games has gone over the total. Shootouts have kept his volume steady and his game script neutral. His efficiency has held with DJ Moore out, too: 10.7 passing EPA in Week 6. The passing is real and sustainable. The fantasy ceiling leans on a rushing touchdown rate no one keeps.

strengths.title: Explosive downfield passing
strengths.body: Throws of 10+ air yards produce 0.599 EPA per attempt. Deep shots run at 0.823 despite a low catch rate, which is what a vertical passer's line should look like. Coleman's emergence as a downfield target gives this a real source rather than a few lucky heaves. Expect it to hold up, with some give-back in the touchdown-to-interception split.

strengths.title: Scrambles that cash in
strengths.body: He scrambles on 8.4% of dropbacks, gaining 191 yards and 12 first downs on 17 tries at 1.247 EPA each. This is the payoff for holding the ball, and it has been part of his game his whole career. It is durable as long as he stays healthy.

strengths.title: Goal-line and short-yardage runner
strengths.body: Designed runs gain little yardage (2.48 per carry) but succeed 69.6% of the time and have scored six times. The Bills use his size as a short-yardage battering ram. The role is sticky, so he will keep getting these touchdown chances even when the rate cools.

concerns.title: Pressures turning into sacks
concerns.body: A 31.3% pressure-to-sack rate ranks 26th. It follows last season's 40.4%, which ranked 47th, after he sat in the teens in 2023-24. It is partly the price of extending plays, and the low pressure rate keeps his overall sack rate near league average. But a defense that gets home more often would expose it.

concerns.title: Rushing TD rate will regress
concerns.body: Eight rushing touchdowns in six games rides on goal-line volume and a hot run of finishes. His 26.9 PPR per game leads the position partly because of it. The role is real, but the rate is not, and his fantasy output should drift down even if his play does not.

concerns.title: Turnover-worthy deep shots
concerns.body: Three of his four interceptions came on 20+ yard throws, and he has four turnover-worthy fumbles on top. His interception rate ranks 29th. That is a cost of the aggressive approach rather than a new flaw, consistent with a career of double-digit interception seasons. His worst game came against the best defense he has faced: Week 3 against a 9th-ranked unit, with 2 interceptions and a 26.9% bad-throw rate.

trend.note: His last three games sit just under his season efficiency (EPA per dropback down 0.022) with his sack rate improving by 2.1 points. Week 3 against the Chargers was the only real dud. His rushing swings wildly week to week, from 121 yards in Week 5 to 1 in Week 6, but the passing has been consistent.

nextGame.headline: Off the bye, home against a defense that leaks deep
nextGame.body:
Baltimore's defense is middle-of-the-pack overall: 16th in EPA and 11th against the pass. It is built to squeeze the short game, allowing -0.154 EPA on short throws (4th), while giving up 0.651 on deep passes (22nd) and 0.64 EPA per target to opposing WR1s (31st). That lines up well with Allen's 2026 vertical lean and less well with the Kincaid underneath game: Baltimore is 5th against TE1s, and tight ends draw a below-league share of targets against it. It has held quarterbacks to one touchdown a game (3rd), so expect efficiency through yardage more than a pile of passing scores.

Availability matters on both sides. Buffalo comes off a 14-day rest at home. DJ Moore's estimated return date is game day itself, so treat him as uncertain; Week 6 showed the passing game holds up without him. For Baltimore, Lamar Jackson is out with an ankle sprain but described as day-to-day. His status shapes the game script: with him, the Ravens offense ranks 7th in EPA against a Bills defense ranked 30th, which points toward another shootout. Without him, the script likely slows. Center Cam Jurgens is also out for Baltimore.

keyMatchups.title: Allen's deep ball vs soft coverage
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore allows 0.651 EPA on deep throws, and Allen is producing 0.823 per deep attempt. With the short area closed off, the vertical shots to Coleman should be the main avenue. The same throws are where his interceptions come from, so this is high-reward, high-variance.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into a strength
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore ranks 4th against short passes and 5th against TE1s. That pressures the Shakir-Kincaid underneath game that drives much of Allen's volume. Expect a lower completion rate and more reliance on chunk plays and scrambles.

keyMatchups.title: Lamar's status sets the script
keyMatchups.body: If Jackson plays, Baltimore's 7th-ranked offense against Buffalo's 30th-ranked defense invites volume and urgency. If he sits, the Bills can lean on their run-leaning tendencies and Allen's short-yardage carries.

nextGame.watch: Whether Jackson is cleared to play. That decides whether this is a shootout or a grind, and whether Allen needs to keep firing deep.

restOfSeason.body:
The passing efficiency is the sturdy part: his intermediate and deep production is backed by a track record of top-ten EPA seasons and a new vertical outlet in Coleman. Expect yards per attempt to drift toward the 8 range rather than stay near 8.8, and expect the deep touchdown-to-interception split to even out somewhat. Projected passing output is 225-265 yards and 1.3-1.8 touchdowns a game, with the Bills' weak defense keeping him throwing in tight games.

The rushing touchdowns are where regression lands. The goal-line role keeps him a threat to score most weeks, but projecting 0.4-0.8 rushing touchdowns a game, rather than his current clip, trims his fantasy line toward the 21-25 point range. That is still at the top of the position. The scramble production and short-yardage usage keep his floor high.
swingFactors: Rushing TD rate near the goal line
DJ Moore's return and Coleman's deep role
Whether pressures keep turning into sacks

confidence.note: Six games and a rushing TD rate that will cool, but the passing profile matches a long track record.
